stem_book: Two particles A and B start from the same point and move in the positive x-direction. In a time interval of 2.00 s after they start, their velocities v vary with time t as shown in the following figures (particle A moves at 2.00 m/s for the first 1.00 s and at 1.00 m/s for the next 1.00 s; for particle B, v rises uniformly from 0 to 2.00 m/s in each 1.00 s interval). What is the maximum separation between the particles during this time interval? (a) 1.00 m (b) 1.25 m (c) 1.50 m (d) 2.00 m
reason: Printed Particle-A graph is only a grid (its velocity line coincides with grid lines, same in the book SB L7 Q10); A's velocity stated in words — the 2-then-1 m/s reading is the only one that gives the key 1.25 m.
